title: Homer: Let the Barts Out
blurb: Extracted, isolated, and stripped of every scrap of context until it means precisely nothing. That is the entire mechanism: the line is not funny inside the episode, and it becomes funny only once nobody can remember what it was originally about. The Simpsons has been supplying this kind of raw material for thirty-five years and shows no sign of exhausting the supply — there is simply too much of it, and too much of it is strange. Play it when a situation calls for a decision nobody understands. Release the Barts.
origin: An out-of-context line from The Simpsons.
